full_text_en:
Qinghai Hongding Real Estate Co., Ltd. v. Qinghai State-owned Assets Investment Management Co., Ltd. and Qinghai Property Rights Exchange Market — dispute over confirmation of contract validity

Ruling Summary

I. Online bidding transactions have the characteristics of immediacy and openness. The property right holder, bidders, and the bidding organizer must strictly abide by the relevant transaction rules. Although the online bidding system automatically generates a Notice of Bidding Result, if it violates the transaction rules and cannot form a valid acceptance, the transaction cannot be established according to law.

II. Online bidding is a special form of auction. Where there are special provisions, those provisions shall prevail; in the absence of special provisions, the general provisions of the Auction Law may apply.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2015) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 351

Appellant (original defendant): Qinghai State-owned Assets Investment Management Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 18, Wei'er Road, Biological Park, Chengbei District, Xining City, Qinghai Province.

Legal Representative: Hao Lihua, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Chen Yan, lawyer of Qinghai Shuren Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Xianli, lawyer of Qinghai Shuren Law Firm.

Appellee (original plaintiff): Qinghai Hongding Real Estate Co., Ltd. Domicile: 20th Floor, Santian Century Plaza, No. 40 West Street, Chengzhong District, Xining City, Qinghai Province.

Legal Representative: Guan Jingwu, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Tang Yimin, employee of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Xing Zhi, lawyer of Beijing Dentons (Xining) Law Firm.

Third party at first instance: Qinghai Property Rights Exchange Market. Domicile: Room 705, Administration Committee Building, Qinghai Biological Science and Technology Industrial Park.

Legal Representative: Shang Guilin, Chairman of the Market.

Agent ad litem: Wu Jianguo, employee of the Market.

The appellant Qinghai State-owned Assets Investment Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the State Investment Company), dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2014) Qing Min Er Chu Zi No. 40 rendered by the Qinghai High People's Court in the case of dispute over confirmation of contract validity with the appellee Qinghai Hongding Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hongding Company) and the original third party Qinghai Property Rights Exchange Market (hereinafter referred to as the Property Rights Exchange Market), filed an appeal with this Court. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with Judge Zhang Xuemei serving as the presiding judge, and Judge Ayiguli and Acting Judge Gao Yanzhu as members, to conduct the trial. Court Clerk Zhang Xijuan served as the recorder. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

The court of first instance found through trial that on December 17, 2010, the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of Qinghai Province approved the entrustment of Lot No. 69 (above-ground structures with a gross floor area of 12,850.84 square meters and land area of 34,505.50 square meters) to the Property Rights Exchange Market for public listing and trading. On July 20, 2011, the State Investment Company submitted an Application for Transfer of Property Rights to the Property Rights Exchange Market, which explained the basic information of the transferor, the basic information of the target enterprise, and the evaluation of the target enterprise. On the same day, the State Investment Company, as Party A, and the Property Rights Exchange Market, as Party B, signed a Property Rights Transfer Service Agreement regarding the transfer of Lot No. 69, entrusting the Property Rights Exchange Market to handle the relevant matters of the above property transfer, with the entrusted matters including: (1) providing consulting services to Party A regarding relevant laws, regulations, policies, and transaction rules; (2) guiding Party A in filling out the Application for Transfer of Property Rights; (3) assisting Party A in formulating internal decision-making documents for the property rights transfer; (4) reviewing documents and materials such as evaluation reports, audit reports, capital verification reports, and legal opinions provided by Party A; (5) being responsible for on-site inspection and verification of the property rights transfer subject matter provided by Party A; (6) entrusting a law firm to review the authenticity, completeness, and legality of the documents and materials provided by Party A and issuing a review opinion; (7) being responsible for formulating and publishing the Announcement on Transfer of Property Rights; (8) being responsible for soliciting and reviewing interested transferees and participating in relevant negotiations; (9) being responsible for jointly determining with Party A the interested transferee and the transaction method; (10) after entering the bidding procedure, being responsible for organizing online bidding activities for public transfer; (11) being responsible for formulating the Property Rights Transaction Contract; (12) ensuring the safety of transaction funds and being responsible for handling the settlement procedures for the property rights transaction price; (13) being responsible for issuing the Property Rights Transaction Certificate; (14) being responsible for supervising the delivery of assets by both parties to the transaction; (15) being responsible for coordinating any disputes arising during the transaction process; (16) providing other services as should be provided in accordance with the property rights transaction rules of the Qinghai Property Rights Exchange Market.

On July 21, September 1, and September 17, 2011, the Property Rights Exchange Market published in the Qinghai Daily, the Xihai Metropolis Daily, and on its website the property rights transfer announcement and online bidding announcement for Lot No. 69, announcing the appraised price of the transfer subject matter, the listing price, conditions for the transferee, the method of online bidding, the deposit payment, and other matters.

On September 20, 2011, the Property Rights Exchange Market used the Jinmajia online bidding system to organize three bidders who participated in the bidding for Lot No. 69. When the bidding entered the time-limited bidding stage, after multiple rounds of bidding, only Hongding Company and Xining Weiye Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Weiye Company) continued with several more rounds of bidding. When Hongding Company bid RMB 28,937,800, Weiye Company's computer page timer stopped counting down at 19 seconds during the time-limited bidding period of 180 seconds. While the Weiye Company operator inquired about the reason and the Property Rights Exchange Market staff provided an explanation, the Jinmajia online bidding system automatically generated a Notice of Bidding Result, with Hongding Company winning Lot No. 69 at a transaction price of RMB 28,937,800, and the bidding process ended.

On September 30, 2011, the Property Rights Exchange Market and Hongding Company affixed their official seals to the above-mentioned Notice of Bidding Result to confirm it, but the State Investment Company did not affix its seal.

On September 22, 2011, the State Investment Company sent to the Property Rights Exchange Market the Letter on Refusing to Confirm the Bidding Result for the Transfer Project of the Land Use Right and Above-Ground Structures at No. 69, South Chuan East Road, Xining City, stating that due to a computer malfunction on the part of one of the bidders during the bidding process, which had an unpredictable impact on the transaction result, the bidding result of that day was not confirmed.

After verifying the operating status of the Jinmajia network with Beijing Guoyan Network Data Technology Co., Ltd., the hosting service provider of the Jinmajia network system server room, and upon receiving a certificate from that company on September 28, 2011, confirming that the network and server had been operating stably, the Property Rights Exchange Market submitted to the State Investment Company on September 30, 2011 the Letter on Determining the Legal Transferee for the Transfer Project of the Land Use Right and Above-Ground Structures at No. 69, South Chuan East Road, Xining City, determining Hongding Company as the legal transferee of the Lot No. 69 transfer project. On the same day, the Property Rights Exchange Market and Hongding Company signed and sealed the Notice of Bidding Result, but the State Investment Company, as the transferor, did not sign or seal the Notice of Bidding Result, and refused to confirm the online bidding result and refused to deliver the assets to Hongding Company, citing the reason that a computer malfunction occurred on the part of a bidder during the bidding activity, which had an unpredictable impact on the transaction result.

The Property Rights Exchange Market is a professional institution for property rights transactions established with the approval of the Qinghai Provincial Government in 1997. Filed with the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of the State Council and the Ministry of Finance, it is the only institution engaged in the transfer of property rights of state-owned enterprises selected and determined by the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of Qinghai Province, and it is also the only institution selected and determined by the Finance Department of Qinghai Province to engage in the disposal of assets of administrative institutions and the transfer of financial enterprise state-owned assets.

The Jinmajia online bidding system is an internet online bidding platform established with joint investment by more than 30 provincial-level property rights trading institutions nationwide and is affiliated with the Beijing Property Rights Exchange. The online bidding activity for this session adopted the "centralized bidding method." Any bidder who passed the transferee qualification review by the Property Rights Exchange Market, registered on the Jinmajia website, applied for bidding, and had their registered account activated could log into the Jinmajia bidding hall to participate in the bidding activity. The "centralized bidding method" process included: 1. Read the instructions; 2. Become an interested bidder through the transferee qualification review by the Property Rights Exchange Market and register an account on the Jinmajia website; 3. Participate in the bidding. The centralized bidding process consisted of a free bidding stage and a time-limited bidding stage. The one-hour period (15:00 to 16:00) after the bidding started was the free bidding stage, during which any bid by a bidder higher than the reserve price was a valid bid. After the free bidding stage ended, the time-limited bidding stage began. The time-limited bidding stage consisted of multiple bidding cycles, with each time-limited bidding cycle lasting three minutes. If no one increased the bid within one time-limited bidding cycle, the current highest bidder would be the buyer of the bidding subject matter, and the bidding activity for that subject matter would end; if someone increased the bid within the time-limited bidding cycle, that bid time would become the starting point of a new time-limited bidding cycle, waiting for new bids, until no new valid bid was made in the last time-limited bidding cycle, and the bidder with the current highest valid bid would become the buyer of the bidding subject matter, and the bidding activity for that subject matter would end; 4. Transaction confirmation. After the bidder successfully bid, the system would automatically pop up a transaction confirmation, and at the same time, the Jinmajia website would send the Notice of Bidding Result to the registered account of that bidder on the Jinmajia website, and the buyer must sign the Property Rights Transaction Contract with the transferor on the day of the successful bid. 5. Settlement and delivery. After signing the Property Rights Transaction Contract, the buyer must pay the transaction price and transaction service fee within the specified time and go through the asset delivery procedures.

Upon the application of both parties, during the original first instance proceedings, this court investigated and collected evidence from Beijing Jinmajia Network Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinmajia Company) regarding the phenomenon of the computer timer stopping during the last 19 seconds of the countdown in the online bidding process organized by the Property Rights Exchange Market for both parties. The company replied in writing to this court, stating that the timer stopping during the last 19 seconds of the countdown was not a network failure but a delay phenomenon on the internet, which could be instantaneously activated and did not affect the bidding behavior. After the bidder Weiye Company reported the issue, the Property Rights Exchange Market staff promptly pointed out that the stopping phenomenon did not affect its bidding and inquired whether it would continue bidding; it indicated that it would not bid further.

On May 17, 2012, Hongding Company filed a lawsuit with the Qinghai High People's Court, requesting: 1. Confirmation that the bidding result of Hongding Company winning the Lot No. 69 transfer project was legal and valid, and that the sales contract between Hongding Company and the State Investment Company was established; 2. An order for the State Investment Company to deliver all assets of Lot No. 69 to Hongding Company and to cooperate with Hongding Company in handling the procedures for changing the asset property rights. All litigation costs of this case were to be borne by the State Investment Company.

The court of first instance held that, based on the parties' claims and defenses, the issues in dispute in this case were: (1) The relationship between the State Investment Company and the Property Rights Exchange Market. (2) Whether the transaction was conducted in accordance with the law and whether the bidding result was valid. (3) Whether the confirmation of the bidding result by the Property Rights Exchange Market could be binding on the State Investment Company. (4) Whether the contract for the transfer of the land use right and above-ground structures in dispute in this case was established in accordance with the law.

(1) Regarding the relationship between the State Investment Company and the Property Rights Exchange Market

This court held that in this case, the State Investment Company, acting pursuant to the approval of the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of Qinghai Province, signed the Property Rights Transfer Service Agreement with the Property Rights Exchange Market and submitted the Application for Transfer of Property Rights. The two parties clearly stipulated their respective rights and obligations, entrusted matters, and the content and method of the transaction in the Property Rights Transfer Service Agreement and the Application for Transfer of Property Rights. From the content of the said agreement, the State Investment Company entrusted the Property Rights Exchange Market to organize the online bidding activity for the transfer subject matter. After entering the bidding procedure, the Property Rights Exchange Market was responsible for organizing the online bidding activity for public transfer, formulating the Property Rights Transaction Contract, handling the settlement procedures for the property rights transaction price, overseeing the delivery of assets by both parties, and coordinating any disputes during the transaction process. The legal relationship between the parties complied with the provisions of Article 65 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC regarding agency by mandate, forming an agency relationship by mandate, i.e., the State Investment Company entrusted the Property Rights Exchange Market to handle the matters of public listing and trading of Lot No. 69.

(2) Whether the transaction was conducted in accordance with the law and whether the bidding result was valid

This court held that the transferor State Investment Company, the bidders Weiye Company and Hongding Company, and the bidding organizer Property Rights Exchange Market all followed the Jinmajia Bidding Hall Usage Rules, the Jinmajia Online Bidding Operation Instructions, and other relevant online bidding operational documents, completing the bidding announcement, Jinmajia account registration, online bidding, and other bidding processes. The entire bidding process did not involve any illegal or irregular circumstances. Although there was a phenomenon of the computer page timer of the operation by Weiye Company stopping during the last 19 seconds of the countdown in the final time-limited bidding stage, Jinmajia Company and Beijing Guoyan Technology Co., Ltd. replied in writing to this court that the 19-second stopping phenomenon was a delay phenomenon on the internet, which did not affect the price increase operation and could be instantaneously restored to normal through a price increase operation. The said stopping phenomenon did not fall within the category of faults that would require the bidding organizer to decide to suspend or terminate the bidding activity as stipulated in the Jinmajia Bidding Hall Usage Rules. Moreover, the on-site staff of the Property Rights Exchange Market explained the timer stopping phenomenon and informed that it did not affect further price increases. As a bidder, Weiye Company should have quoted prices in accordance with the Jinmajia online bidding rules, promptly operated according to the market staff's reminder regarding the internet delay phenomenon, and bear the adverse legal consequences if it failed to operate in a timely manner. Hongding Company quoted a price of RMB 28,937,800 in accordance with the Jinmajia bidding rules, which constituted an offer, and the bidding result automatically generated by the Jinmajia system constituted an acceptance. As a bidder, Hongding Company had no fault in the bidding process as it followed the transaction rules. According to Article 3 of the Auction Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the Auction Law), "Auction is a method of sale in which a specific item or property right is transferred to the highest bidder through public bidding." Article 38 stipulates, "The buyer means the bidder who purchases the auction subject matter at the highest bid." Article 51 stipulates, "The auction is concluded when the highest bid of the bidder is confirmed by the auctioneer's hammer drop or other public indication of purchase." Under the premise that the above-mentioned stopping phenomenon was not a fault issue, the bidding result generated by the Jinmajia online bidding system should be found to be lawful and valid. Furthermore, the final bidding result of this transaction was produced after 16 rounds of bidding by three bidders. The State Investment Company's argument that the stopping during the last 19 seconds affected the price increase and that full competition was not achieved could not be sustained.

(3) Whether the confirmation of the bidding result by the Property Rights Exchange Market could be binding on the State Investment Company

This court held that, according to Article 3, Item (9) of the Property Rights Transfer Agreement signed between the Property Rights Exchange Market and the State Investment Company, the Property Rights Exchange Market was responsible for jointly determining with the State Investment Company the interested transferee and the transaction method. Item (10) stipulated that after entering the bidding procedure, the Property Rights Exchange Market was responsible for organizing the online bidding activity for public transfer. The State Investment Company's Application for Transfer of Property Rights expressly stated that if, after the listing period, two or more qualified interested transferees were collected, the online bidding method would be selected to determine the transferee. The State Investment Company entrusted the Property Rights Exchange Market to conduct public bidding using the Jinmajia online bidding method, and ultimately the transferee was determined by the Jinmajia online bidding method. As discussed above, the bidding result generated by the Jinmajia online bidding system was lawful and valid. The act of the Property Rights Exchange Market in confirming and delivering the Notice of Bidding Result to Hongding Company was a matter entrusted by the Property Rights Transfer Service Agreement, and the Property Rights Exchange Market, after verifying the operating status of the Jinmajia network with Beijing Guoyan Network Data Technology Co., Ltd. and, upon receiving a certificate from that company on September 28, 2011, confirming that the network and server had been operating stably on the day of the transaction, delivered the Notice of Bidding Result to Hongding Company. This confirmation act by the Property Rights Exchange Market did not exceed the scope of authorization granted by the State Investment Company to the Property Rights Exchange Market and was binding on the State Investment Company. Under the premise that the listing transaction rules were jointly determined by the parties involved to be applicable, the transaction process did not involve any illegal or irregular circumstances, and the transaction result was lawful and valid, the State Investment Company's refusal to confirm the result on the grounds that the transaction process did not achieve full competition would undermine the stability of online bidding. The State Investment Company's argument that the Property Rights Exchange Market had no authority to confirm the transaction result could not be sustained and was not supported.

(4) Whether the contract for the transfer of the land use right and above-ground structures in dispute in this case was established in accordance with the law

This court held that the State Investment Company, through the Property Rights Transfer Service Agreement, entrusted the Property Rights Exchange Market to issue an invitation to offer for the transfer of Lot No. 69. The bidders Weiye Company and Hongding Company submitted offers for the price of the subject matter through online bidding. The State Investment Company made an acceptance through the specific transaction method of the Jinmajia trading system. The bidding result of RMB 28,937,800 quoted by Hongding Company, automatically generated by the Jinmajia system, constituted the acceptance of the State Investment Company, and this acceptance was lawful and valid. Article 25 of the Contract Law of the PRC provides that a contract is established when the acceptance takes effect. Moreover, in terms of the content of the online bidding announcement result of this case, it included the names of the parties, the subject matter, the quantity, and the price, which were the main content of the Property Rights Transaction Contract to be signed by the parties, and it complied with the provisions of Article 1, Paragraph 1 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation (II) of the Contract Law of the PRC: "If a dispute between parties arises as to whether a contract is established, and the people's court can determine the name or names of the parties, the subject matter, and the quantity, the contract shall generally be deemed to be established, unless otherwise provided by law or agreed by the parties." Therefore, the sales contract between the State Investment Company and Hongding Company for Lot No. 69 should be deemed established, and the parties should continue to perform the contract.

In conclusion, this court held that the online bidding result in this case was lawful and valid, and the sales contract between the State Investment Company and Hongding Company was established in accordance with the law. The parties should continue to perform the contract. Pursuant to Article 25, Article 130, and Article 173 of the Contract Law of the PRC, Article 1, Paragraph 1 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation (II) of the Contract Law of the PRC, and Articles 3, 31, 51, 52, and 55 of the Auction Law, and Article 142 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, and after discussion by the judicial committee of this court, the judgment was as follows: 1. The online bidding result of the land use right and above-ground structures at No. 69, South Chuan East Road, Xining City, organized by the Qinghai Property Rights Exchange Market on September 20, 2011, for the Qinghai State-owned Assets Investment Management Co., Ltd., was lawful and valid, and the sales contract between Qinghai Hongding Real Estate Co., Ltd. and Qinghai State-owned Assets Investment Management Co., Ltd. for the above-mentioned subject matter was established; 2. Qinghai State-owned Assets Investment Management Co., Ltd. shall deliver the land and above-ground structures (including relevant title documents) at No. 69, South Chuan East Road, Xining City, to Qinghai Hongding Real Estate Co., Ltd. within ten days after this judgment takes effect. The case acceptance fee of RMB 186,489 shall be borne by Qinghai State-owned Assets Investment Management Co., Ltd.

Guotou Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment above, appealed, submitting the following: 1. The basis applied in the first-instance judgment seriously contravenes the transaction rules in this case. The parties participating in the transaction in this case agreed to operate in accordance with documents related to online bidding, such as the "Jinmajia Bidding Hall Usage Rules," but the first-instance judgment applied the "Auction Law of the PRC" as the basis for the transaction. The transaction procedures, methods, and requirements stipulated in the "Auction Law of the PRC" are completely different from the agreements among the parties in this case, and the "Auction Law of the PRC" should not be applied to this case. 2. The conditions for the formation of the transaction in this case are completely different from the findings of the first-instance judgment. The first-instance judgment found that the bidding result generated by the Jinmajia online bidding system constituted an acceptance, which violates the content of the "Jinmajia Online Bidding Operation Instructions." According to the agreements in documents such as the "Jinmajia Online Bidding Operation Instructions," the "confirmation of transaction" in this online bidding process is that the successful bidder wins the bid, the system pops up a transaction prompt, the Jinmajia website sends the "Bidding Result Notice" to the account of that successful bidder, and the successful bidder and the transferor sign the "Property Rights Transaction Contract." 3. The first-instance judgment's determination that the sale contract was formed conflicts with legal provisions. The "Urban Real Estate Administration Law of the PRC," the "Interim Regulations of the PRC on the Assignment and Transfer of the Right to Use State-owned Land in Cities and Towns," and the "Interim Measures for the Administration of the Transfer of State-owned Property Rights of Enterprises" provide that the transfer of the subject matter in this case must be in the form of a written transfer contract. Since no written agreement was signed for this transaction, the sale contract was not formed. 4. The first-instance judgment's determination regarding the handling of the network issue violates the transaction rules and legal provisions. The first-instance judgment's finding that "the staff of the Property Rights Market promptly pointed out that the stoppage phenomenon did not affect its bidding, and asked whether it wished to continue bidding, and it expressed that it would no longer bid" is not supported by evidence. The first-instance judgment found that Jinmajia Company and Beijing Guoyan Technology Company replied in writing that the 19-second stoppage phenomenon was a normal occurrence on the internet and did not affect the price-add operation. The aforementioned stoppage of the timer did not fall within the scope of faults specified in the online bidding rules that would warrant the suspension or termination of the bidding activity. This finding does not comply with Article 29 of the "Jinmajia Online Bidding Hall Usage Rules," nor does it comply with the interpretation rules for standard form contracts as stipulated in Articles 39 and 41 of the "Contract Law of the PRC." In summary, the appellant requests that the first-instance judgment be reversed, all claims of the appellee be dismissed, and the appellee bear all litigation costs.

Hongding Company responded in its defense, stating: 1. The first-instance court correctly applied the "Auction Law of the PRC." (1) Guidance on the applicable rules for this case from current normative documents. According to the provisions of Article 17 of the "Interim Measures for the Administration of the Transfer of State-owned Property Rights of Enterprises" and Article 21 of the "Qinghai Province Measures for the Administration of State-owned Property Rights of Enterprises," the relationship among the parties in this transaction should be adjusted by applying the "Auction Law of the PRC." (2) Online bidding activities are a form of auction activity. The first-instance court's application of the "Auction Law of the PRC" as the basis for adjudicating this case is in line with legislative intent. (3) The conditions for the formation of a contract under the "Auction Law of the PRC" are entirely consistent with the conditions for the formation of a contract stipulated in the "Jinmajia Bidding Hall Usage Rules" and the "Jinmajia Online Bidding Operation Instructions," and there is no conflict. There is no situation where the first-instance court chose to apply the "Auction Law of the PRC" as the basis for judgment in order to circumvent the aforementioned two bidding rules. 2. Regarding the conditions for the formation of the transaction. The "Jinmajia Online Bidding Operation Instructions" stipulate, "The successful bidder shall sign the 'Property Rights Transaction Contract' with the transferor on the day after the bidding transaction is concluded." According to this provision, "after conclusion" is a condition for signing the written contract. In other words, signing the "Property Rights Transaction Contract" is a task after the formation of the contract between the parties, not a condition for the formation of the contract. Consistent with this view are the provisions of Article 17 of the "Interim Measures for the Administration of the Transfer of State-owned Property Rights of Enterprises," which state, "After the transaction for the transfer of state-owned property rights of an enterprise is concluded, the transferor and the transferee shall sign a property rights transfer contract, ..." and Article 23 of the "Qinghai Province Measures for the Administration of State-owned Property Rights of Enterprises," which state, "After the transaction for the transfer of state-owned property rights of an enterprise is concluded, the transferor and the transferee shall sign a property rights transfer contract, ..." Therefore, since the transaction between the parties has already been concluded, it means that the sale contract between the parties has already been formed. Whether the parties sign a written contract is unrelated to whether the contract is formed. In this case, the real estate transaction contract was signed in electronic form, and an electronic transaction contract is a special form of written contract. 3. Regarding the so-called "handling of the network issue." (1) Regardless of whether the timer lag phenomenon occurred in the bidding system at the time of the incident, the consequences arising from this phenomenon cannot be borne by Hongding Company. Hongding Company had no fault in this bidding activity. The claim by Guotou Company that the Property Rights Market improperly handled the matter, thereby rendering the entire bidding result invalid, is entirely untenable. Even if Guotou Company believes there is a dispute with the Property Rights Market, it cannot deny the fact that Hongding Company, as a faultless bidder, successfully won the bid. (2) Guotou Company is not entitled to raise objections to the bidding result. According to the provisions of the "Interim Measures for the Administration of the Transfer of State-owned Property Rights of Enterprises" and the "Qinghai Province Measures for the Administration of State-owned Property Rights of Enterprises," only the state-owned assets supervision and administration institution or the approving authority for the transfer of enterprise property rights has the right to raise objections to the validity of transactions involving state-owned property rights of enterprises. Guotou Company has no right to raise objections regarding the validity of the transaction. (3) The various bidding rules involved in this case were all formulated and released by Guotou Company and the Property Rights Market. If there are different interpretations, they should be interpreted in a manner unfavorable to Guotou Company. In summary, the appellee requests that the appeal be dismissed and the original judgment be affirmed.

The third party at first instance, the Property Rights Market, submitted its opinion, stating: 1. The Property Rights Market is a lawfully established and legally operated institution for the transfer of state-owned property rights. The conduct of the Property Rights Market is subject to the relevant provisions of the "Auction Law of the PRC." The Property Rights Market is the only designated institution for the transfer of state-owned property rights in Qinghai Province. It lawfully accepted the entrustment of Guotou Company and, with its written consent, proceeded to dispose of the assets to be transferred by Guotou Company through online bidding. This online bidding activity fully conforms to the definition of "auction" in the "Auction Law of the PRC," which states, "Auction refers to a method of sale whereby specific items or property rights are transferred to the highest bidder through public bidding." Therefore, this activity should be subject to the adjustment of the "Auction Law of the PRC." 2. The conditions for the formation of the transaction. According to the principles of contract law, in online bidding, when the electronic acceptance reaches the computer system used by the bidder, the sale contract between the parties is formed. As for Guotou Company's understanding that the contract is only formed upon signing a written contract, this is completely inconsistent with the transaction rules jointly formulated by Guotou Company and the Property Rights Market. In particular, it should be noted that the transaction rules explicitly state that the written contract is signed only after the transaction is concluded between the parties. This makes it clear that before the signing of the written contract, the contract between the parties has already been formed, and no separate confirmation is required. 3. The use of electronic contract forms for real estate transactions complies with legal provisions. Currently, all state-owned property rights trading institutions in China choose the form of online bidding for transactions, including a large number of real estate transactions. Property rights trading institutions across the country and administrative departments for real estate all recognize the common knowledge that electronic contracts are a special form of written contract. 4. The Property Rights Market's procedures for handling this bidding were legal and proper, without any impropriety. Guotou Company does not have the standing to raise objections. In summary, the Property Rights Market requests that Guotou Company's appeal be dismissed.

During the second-instance trial of this court, Guotou Company submitted the trial transcript of the Xining Arbitration Commission dated December 14, 2011, to prove that the Property Rights Market had clearly stated during the trial of the dispute over the property rights transfer service agreement with Guotou Company that the timer stoppage was a fact. Upon cross-examination during the second-instance trial, Hongding Company confirmed the authenticity of this evidence but argued that it did not constitute new evidence. The Property Rights Market confirmed the authenticity of this evidence but did not recognize its purpose of proof. Since all parties had no objection to the authenticity of the above evidence, this court confirms its authenticity.

Except for the fact that the staff of the Property Rights Market asked Weiye Company whether it wished to continue bidding and Weiye Company indicated it would no longer bid, the second instance confirms the facts found by the first instance. Additionally, the following facts are found:

On September 21, 2011, Weiye Company entrusted Qinghai Shuren Law Firm to send a letter to the Property Rights Market, stating: According to your market's prior instructions and explanations, after the free bidding time ended, the limited-time bidding phase began. During the limited-time bidding phase, Weiye Company, as an意向受让方, had the right to bid within a 180-second period. However, during the limited-time bidding phase, after another party had bid, when the timer of the Jinmajia online bidding system counted down to 19 seconds, the timer stopped counting down. The personnel of Weiye Company who were present at the bidding site immediately discovered the above situation and requested your market's assigned technical staff, Fan Qiang, to handle it. After confirming that the timer had stopped counting down, your market's technical staff, Fan Qiang, was about to handle it when the Jinmajia online bidding system displayed a prompt indicating the end of the bidding. Due to the stoppage of the timer countdown, Weiye Company lost its bidding opportunity within the remaining 19 seconds. In view of the above situation, please provide a timely reply on how to protect Weiye Company's right to participate in the bidding for the transfer project of the land use right and above-ground attachments at No. 69 Nanchuan West Road. At the same time, Weiye Company reserves the right to take corresponding measures to protect all its lawful rights and interests.

On December 5, 2011, the "Reply Letter of Weiye Company Regarding the 'Notice Letter'" stated: 1. This company does not confirm the online bidding process and result for the public transfer of the land use right and above-ground attachments at No. 69 Nanchuan East Road, Xining City, held at 15:00 on September 20, 2011; 2. This company requests your market to reorganize the bidding for the transfer project of the land use right and above-ground attachments at No. 69 Nanchuan East Road, Xining City, in accordance with relevant national laws, regulations, and transaction rules; 3. This company reserves the right to take lawful measures to protect all its lawful rights and interests.

It was further found that during the trial of the arbitration case concerning the dispute over the property rights transfer service agreement between the Property Rights Market and Guotou Company, the arbitrator asked the Property Rights Market: "Was there a phenomenon of the countdown stopping for 19 seconds? Were the confirmations of abandonment of online bidding all signed?" The Property Rights Market answered: "The stoppage for 19 seconds is a fact. Three out of the four parties signed, but Weiye Company did not."

This court holds that the issue in dispute in the second instance is whether the sale contract between Guotou Company and Hongding Company regarding the subject matter at No. 69 was formed and what its validity is. Based on the opinions of the parties, the analysis is conducted from the following three aspects:

1. Regarding the transaction rules to be followed in the transaction in question

In this case, Guotou Company, as Party A, and the Property Rights Market, as Party B, signed the "Property Rights Transfer Service Agreement" for the transfer of the subject matter at No. 69, whereby Guotou Company entrusted the Property Rights Market to handle the relevant matters concerning the transfer of the above property. On September 19 and September 20, 2011, the Property Rights Market respectively signed the "Online Bidding Agreement" with Weiye Company and Hongding Company, stipulating the two companies' participation in the online bidding activity for the transfer project of the subject matter at No. 69. All parties conducting transactions for the subject matter at No. 69 using the Jinmajia online bidding system at the Property Rights Market should abide by the transaction rules. The "Jinmajia Online Bidding Operation Instructions" and the "Jinmajia Online Bidding Hall Usage Rules" are both important components of these transaction rules.

In the second instance, Hongding Company and the Property Rights Market claimed that the "Jinmajia Online Bidding Hall Usage Rules" submitted by Guotou Company did not match the publicly disclosed documents, and that the "Jinmajia Bidding Hall Usage Rules" issued by the Property Rights Market and Hongding Company were the original texts sent to all bidders. Regarding this issue, this court holds: First, in the first instance, both Hongding Company and Guotou Company submitted the "Jinmajia Online Bidding Hall Usage Rules" as evidence and expressed their opinions on the evidence, and neither party disputed its authenticity. Second, in the first instance of this case, Guotou Company also submitted this evidence, and Hongding Company and the Property Rights Market did not raise objections to its authenticity. Third, in its reply to the first-instance court during the first instance, Jinmajia Company also stated that the rule system governing each online bidding activity is composed of the "Jinmajia Online Bidding Hall Usage Rules," the "Transaction Instructions" of the organizing party, and other relevant rule documents. Finally, from the name, the "Jinmajia Online Bidding Hall Usage Rules," as opposed to the "Jinmajia Bidding Hall Usage Rules," should be special rules applicable to online bidding, and the two are not in conflict. Therefore, although Hongding Company and the Property Rights Market raised objections to the authenticity of the "Jinmajia Online Bidding Hall Usage Rules" in the second instance, they failed to provide evidence to overturn their previous opinions on the evidence. This court does not accept this defense and shall determine that the "Jinmajia Online Bidding Hall Usage Rules" are a component of the transaction rules for the online bidding in this case. Regarding the issue of whether the "Auction Law of the PRC" should apply, this court holds that online bidding is a special form of auction. Where there are special provisions, those provisions shall prevail; where there are no special provisions, the general provisions of the "Auction Law of the PRC" may apply.

2. Regarding the issue of whether there was a fact of the timer stopping when the countdown reached 19 seconds

In the second instance of this case, the parties disputed the existence of the fact of the timer stopping. However, during the trial of the arbitration case concerning the dispute over the property rights transfer service agreement between the Property Rights Market and Guotou Company, the Property Rights Market clearly stated that the countdown stopping for 19 seconds was a fact. In the second-instance trial of this case, the Property Rights Market also acknowledged that due to the dispute on the day of the transaction, it had organized consultations among all parties. In light of the facts that Weiye Company entrusted Qinghai Shuren Law Firm to send a letter to the Property Rights Market on September 21, 2011, and that Weiye Company again sent a letter to the Property Rights Market on December 5, 2011, raising objections to the timer stoppage, as well as the fact that Guotou Company sent a letter to the Property Rights Market stating that due to a computer malfunction at one of the bidders during the bidding process, it did not confirm the bidding result of that day, it should be determined that during the online bidding transaction in this case, there was a fact of the countdown timer stopping. Although Hongding Company and the Property Rights Market argued that this fact did not exist, they did not provide sufficient evidence to prove it. Therefore, this court does not accept this defense.

3. Regarding the issue of whether the stoppage of the timer resulted in the transaction in dispute not being formed

According to the "Jinmajia Online Bidding Operation Instructions," the limited-time bidding phase consists of multiple bidding cycles, each limited-time bidding cycle being 3 minutes. Bidders have the right to submit new bids within the complete 3-minute bidding cycle. Article 29 of the "Jinmajia Online Bidding Hall Usage Rules" stipulates that the organizing party has the right to suspend or terminate the bidding activity in any of the following circumstances: (1) Failure of the Jinmajia server room network, the internet, or the organizing party's network; ... (4) Failure of a client terminal when participating in the bidding activity through the organizing party's designated terminal; ...

In this case, during the online bidding for the subject matter at No. 69, when Weiye Company was in the bidding phase with a limited time of 180 seconds, the timer on its computer page stopped counting down at 19 seconds remaining. When the staff of the Property Rights Market was handling the situation, the Jinmajia online bidding system automatically generated the "Bidding Result Notice." Weiye Company sent a letter to the Property Rights Market stating that during the limited-time bidding phase, the timer stopped counting down, causing Weiye Company to lose its bidding opportunity within the remaining 19 seconds. Although in the first instance, the parties submitted a written testimony of Fan Qiang stating that after being alerted by the bidder Weiye Company, Fan Qiang promptly pointed out that the stoppage phenomenon did not affect their bidding and asked whether they wished to continue bidding, and they indicated they would no longer bid. However, Fan Qiang, without justifiable reason, did not appear in court to testify. Moreover, he was a staff member of the Property Rights Market who was guiding Weiye Company in the online bidding transaction in dispute at that time and had an interest in the Property Rights Market, a party in this case. His testimony conflicted with the content of Weiye Company's letter and cannot be used alone as a basis for determining the facts of the case. Jinmajia Company and Beijing Guoyan Technology Company replied in writing that the 19-second stoppage phenomenon was a delay phenomenon on the internet and did not affect the price-add operation. By performing a price-add operation, normalcy could be restored instantly. However, during the second-instance trial, the Property Rights Market stated that the timer stoppage phenomenon in this case was an abnormal phenomenon and was the first system delay encountered by the Property Rights Market when using the system. At the same time, it acknowledged that it had not trained bidders on how to respond to such unexpected situations. Therefore, even if, as Jinmajia Network Company claimed, this phenomenon did not affect normal price addition, Weiye Company was unaware that normal price addition was still possible under such exceptional circumstances and was unaware of how to operate. Given that Weiye Company explicitly raised objections, the claim by Hongding Company and the Property Rights Market that the timer stoppage phenomenon did not, in fact, affect the transaction lacks sufficient basis. This court holds that online bidding transactions are characterized by immediacy and openness, and their transaction rules are stringent. The property owner, bidders, and the organizing party of the bidding must all strictly comply with them. In this case, given the fact of the timer stoppage and the objections raised by both Weiye Company and Guotou Company that this fact prevented full bidding, it should be determined that the timer stoppage phenomenon resulted in the transaction in question not achieving full bidding.

In its written reply, Jinmajia Company also stated that the network delay that occurred in this bidding activity did not fall within the category of a fault. Jinmajia Company provided network services for the online bidding activity in this case and has an interest in the case. The explanations and interpretations it provided regarding whether the timer stoppage phenomenon in the transaction in question constituted a fault have low probative value. Moreover, regardless of whether the timer stoppage phenomenon constituted a fault, the transaction in question violated the rule that "during the limited-time bidding phase, bidders should be given a complete bidding cycle to achieve full bidding." The first-instance judgment's determination that the bidding result in this case was lawful and valid, on the premise that the stoppage phenomenon did not constitute a fault, was improper, and this court corrects that.

In summary, in this case, although the Jinmajia online bidding system automatically generated the "Bidding Result Notice," because the transaction in question violated the transaction rules and did not form an effective acceptance, it is not binding on Guotou Company, and the transaction was not formed. The defenses raised by Hongding Company, that the Property Rights Market acted as an agent for Guotou Company and that its expressions of intent are binding on Guotou Company, and that Hongding Company, as a bona fide third party, resulted in the valid formation of the sale contract, are all untenable. Guotou Company's grounds for appeal, that the transaction in this case is invalid and the sale contract was not formed, are established. In accordance with the provisions of Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item 2 of the "Civil Procedure Law of the PRC," this court hereby renders the following judgment:

1. Reverse the Civil Judgment No. 40 (2014) of the Second Civil Division of the Qinghai High People's Court;

2. Dismiss all claims of Qinghai Hongding Real Estate Co., Ltd.

The case acceptance fees for the first instance and the second instance, each amounting to RMB 186,489, shall be borne by Qinghai Hongding Real Estate Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
